questions.q:
Given below are two statements :
Statement-I: The reactance of an ac circuit is zero. It is possible that the circuit contains a capacitor and an inductor.
Statement-II: In ac circuit, the average power delivered by the source never becomes zero.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The reactance of a circuit containing a capacitor and an inductor is given by& $X = {X}_{L} - {X}_{C} = \omegaL - \dfrac{1}{\omegaC}$. An AC circuit has zero reactance at resonance, i.e., when,~${X}_{L} = {X}_{C}$. So, first statement is true.

The power consumption in an AC circuit is zero when circuit contains only inductance or capacitance since average power consumed in a cycle is zero for inductance or capacitance. So, second statement is false.

questions.q: The angular frequency of alternating current in a L-C-R circuit is $100rads^{- 1}$. The components connected are shown in the figure. Find the value of inductance of the coil and capacity of condenser.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Current through $60Ω$ resistance $= \dfrac{15}{60} = \dfrac{1}{4}A$

thus capacitor current $= \dfrac{1}{4}A$

$∵ {V}_{C} = I{X}_{C}$

$10 = \dfrac{1}{4} \times \dfrac{1}{\omegaC}$

$∴ C = \dfrac{1}{40\omega} = \dfrac{1}{4000} = 250\muF$

Now,

current through $40Ω$ resistance $= \dfrac{20}{40} = \dfrac{1}{2}A$

thus current through inductor $= \dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{4} = \dfrac{1}{4}A$

${V}_{L} = I{X}_{L} = \dfrac{1}{4} \times \omegaL$

$20 = \dfrac{1}{4} \times 100 \times L$

$⇒ L = 0 . 8H$

questions.q: In a series $LR$ circuit with ${X}_{L} = R$,~power factor is ${P}_{1}$. If a capacitor of capacitance $C$ with ${X}_{C} = {X}_{L}$ is added to the circuit the power factor becomes ${P}_{2}$. The ratio of ${P}_{1}$ to ${P}_{2}$ will be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
In case of& $LR$~circuit:

Given:~${X}_{L} = R$

${P}_{1} = cosϕ = \dfrac{R}{Z} = \dfrac{R}{R^{2} + \left({X}_{L}\right)2} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

In case of~$LCR$~circuit:

${P}_{2} = cosϕ = \dfrac{R}{Z} = \dfrac{R}{R^{2} + \left({X}_{L} - {X}_{C}\right)2} = 1$

Therefore,

$\dfrac{P1}{P2} = 1: \sqrt{2}$

questions.q: An alternating voltage $V ( t ) = 220\sin \left(100\pit\right)$ volt is applied to a purely resistive load of $50Ω . The time taken for the current to rise from half of the peak value to the peak value is:$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$i = \dfrac{V}{R} = \dfrac{220}{50}\sin \left(100\pit\right)$
$\text{i} = {i}_\maxsin \left(100\pit\right)$
For $\text{i} = \dfrac{imax}{2}:$
$\dfrac{imax}{2} = {i}_\maxsin \left(100\pit\right)$
$\sin 100\pit = $\dfrac{1}{2}$⇒ 100\pit = $\dfrac{π}{6}
$t = $\dfrac{1}{600}$s$
For $i = {i}_\max:$
${i}_\max = {i}_\maxsin \l$left(100\pi$t)$
$\sin 100\pit = 1 ⇒ 100\pit = $\dfrac{\pi}{2}
$⇒ t = $\dfrac{1}{200}$s$

so time for~\dfrac{imax}{2}$to{i}_\max$~is~
${t}_{( {i}_\max )} - $t\left(\dfrac{imax}{2}\right) = \dfrac{1}{200} - \dfrac{1}{600} = \dfrac{1}{300} =$3.33ms^{}

$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Potential energy stored in inductor is given by& $U = \dfrac{1}{2}L^{2}$

$\cup ∝ l^{2}$

$\dfrac{U}{U0} = \left(\dfrac{1}{I0}\right)2$

$\dfrac{1}{n} = \left(\dfrac{1}{I0}\right)2$

$\dfrac{1}{I0} = 1 - e^{- RT / L} = \dfrac{1}{n}$

$t = \dfrac{L}{R}ln\dfrac{n}{\sqrt{n} - 1}$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I : An AC circuit undergoes electrical resonance if it contains either a capacitor or an inductor.

Statement II: An AC circuit containing a pure capacitor or a pure inductor consumes high power due to its non-zero power factor. In the light of above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Statement I is false but statement II is true
Statement I is true but statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For resonance to occur& the condition is& ${X}_{L} = {X}_{C}$.

So, both inductor and capacitor is~required.

The power factor is given by~$cosϕ$.

For an inductor the power factor is zero-lagging,~$\cos 90 ° = 0$. The angle between the voltage and current is~$90 °$.

For a capacitor the power factor is zero-leading.

Hence, both statements are false.

questions.q: The equation of current in a purely inductive circuit is $5\sin \left(49\pit - 30 °\right)$. If the inductance is $30mH then the equation for the voltage across the inductor, will be$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
In inductive circuit, the voltage leads the current by& $90 °$. Therefore,

${ϕ}_{0V} - {ϕ}_{0I} = 90 ° ⇒ {ϕ}_{0V} = 60 °$

From the given equation~$5\sin \left(49\pit - 30 °\right)$, angular frequency~$\omega =49\pi rads^{- 1}$

The amplitude of the voltage across the inductor will be,

${V}_{0} = {i}_{0}{X}_{L}$

$⇒ {V}_{0} = {i}_{0} \left(\omegaL\right)$

$⇒ {V}_{0} = \left(5\right)\l$left(49\pi) \left($30 $\times {10}^{- 3}\right)=$23 . 1$~

$⇒ V = 23 . $1\sin \left($49\pit + 60 °\right)

$

questions.q: In a series $LR$ circuit ${X}_{L} = R$ and power factor of the circuit is ${P}_{1}$. When capacitor with capacitance $C$ such that ${X}_{L} = {X}_{C}$ is put in series, the power factor becomes ${P}_{2}$. The ratio $\dfrac{P1}{P2}$ is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
In case of $L - R$ circuit

$Z = \sqrt{{XL}^{2} + R^{2}}$~Therefore,~power factor

${P}_{1} = cosϕ = \dfrac{R}{Z}$

As ${X}_{L} = R$~$⇒ Z = \sqrt{2}R$

$⇒ {P}_{1} = \dfrac{R}{\sqrt{2}R} ⇒ {P}_{1} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

In case of $L - C - R$~circuit

$Z = \sqrt{R^{2} + \left({X}_{L} - {X}_{C}\right)2}$

According to the question~${X}_{L} = {X}_{C}$~$⇒ Z = R⇒ {P}_{2} = cosϕ = \dfrac{R}{R} = 1$

$⇒ \dfrac{P1}{P2} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Ratio of EMF developed will be given by,

questions.q: In a series LCR circuit, the inductive reactance  \left({X}_{L}\right)$ is $10Ω$ and the capacitive reactance  \left({X}_{C}\right)$ is $4Ω$. The resistance $( R )$ in the circuit is $6Ω$. The power factor of the circuit is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
We know that power factor is $cosϕ$,

$cosϕ = \dfrac{R}{Z} . . . \left(1\right)$

$Z = $\sqrt{R^{2} + \left({X}_{L} - {X}_{C}\right)2} . . . \left(2\right)$

$⇒ Z = \sqrt{{6}^{2} + ( 10 - 4{)}^{2}}$

$⇒ Z = 6\sqrt{2}∣ cosϕ = \dfrac{6}{6\sqrt{2}}$

$cosϕ = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$

questions.solution:
Just after closing the switch $S$, inductor behaves like an open circuit, so no current will flow through~$2Ω$~resistors.

questions.q: A series LCR circuit is connected to an AC source of $220V$, $50$ Hz. The circuit contains a resistance $R = 80Ω$, an inductor of inductive reactance ${X}_{L} = 70Ω$, and a capacitor of capacitive reactance ${X}_{C} = 130Ω$. The power factor of circuit is~$\dfrac{x}{10}$.~The value of $x$ is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Power factor in LCR circuit is given by,&

$cosϕ = \dfrac{R}{Z}$, where,~$Z$~is~the total impedance of the circuit.

So,~$cosϕ = \dfrac{R}{R^{2} + \left({X}_{C} - {X}_{L}\right)2}$

Putting the values, we have

$⇒ cosϕ = \dfrac{80}{( 80{)}^{2} + ( 60{)}^{2}}$

$⇒ cosϕ = \dfrac{80}{100} ⇒ \dfrac{8}{10}$

Thus, the value of~$x = 8$.

questions.q: An inductor of self inductance 1 H connected in series with a resistor of $100 \pi \mathrm{ohm}$ and an ac supply of $100 \pi$ volt, 50 Hz. Maximum current flowing in the circuit is ________ A.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Impedance of circuit
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{Z}=\sqrt{\mathrm{R}^2+\left(\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{L}}\right)^2}=\sqrt{\mathrm{R}^2+\left(\omega_{\mathrm{L}}\right)^2} \\ & =\sqrt{(100 \pi)^2+(2 \pi \times 50 \times 1)^2} \\ & =\sqrt{(100 \pi)^2+(100 \pi)^2} \\ & =\sqrt{2} \times 100 \pi \\ & \mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{rms}}=\frac{V}{2}=\frac{100 \pi}{\sqrt{2} \times 100 \pi}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ & \mathrm{I}_{\max }=\sqrt{2} \mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{rms}}=\sqrt{2} \times \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}=1 \text { Ampere }
\end{aligned}$
Correct Answer : 1
